page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 64 dedicated physical cores using the AWS Neoverse-V1 model running at 2.6 GHz, with one thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 3800 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Network performance is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 30 Gbps, managed via the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-core and memory subsystem capabilities. The instance achieves a strong multi-core CPU performance score of 97904.32 in stress-ng and a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3160.9. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 6200.09 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 253.52 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations are also a strength, with PassMark database operations scoring in the top 25% and Redis SET operations reaching 101.36 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is average, and text generation for small LLM models is poor at 9.82 tokens per second, though medium model text generation remains strong at 30.27 tokens per second.

The r7gd.16xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency by combining high-density ARM-based compute resources with a large memory footprint and high-speed local NVMe storage. This resource density reduces the need for external block storage attachments, optimizing data-intensive workloads. The instance is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, caching layers like Redis, large-scale data processing, and web serving applications requiring high throughput.
